name: law_firm_software_007_time_entry_invoice_conversion
instruction: Run the firm's priority invoice generation batch, per firm policy BILL-GEN-01 (in firm_policies), batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta), as of the episode date. The policy defines which matters make this batch (the episode row's top_n, ranked by approved work -- with written-off work and zero-rate entries never billed), how invoices are numbered and dated (the episode row's due_offset_days sets the payment terms), and which time entries flip once their invoice exists. Before touching anything, snapshot the firm's work in progress: one ops_reports row per matter carrying approved work under report='wip_snapshot', with that matter's approved value and entry count as it stands BEFORE the batch. After generating the invoices and flipping exactly the entries each invoice covers, push one ops_reports realization-impact row (report='realization_impact') showing the firm's realization -- measured the way the firm's KPI policy (KPI-REAL-01) defines it -- before the batch versus after, and one ops_reports exception row (report='billing_exceptions') accounting for the matters that carried approved work but fell outside this batch's cut. No other ops_reports rows for this batch_code under those report names may exist. Only invoices, time_entries, and ops_reports may be touched. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: top-N cut boundary: matters ranked just outside the episode row's top_n (10-20) carry real approved work and must NOT be billed; snapshot background: 1914 matters carry approved value, so 'bill everything with approved time' balloons into thousands of invoices -- the cut keeps the write set bounded while still requiring a full firm-wide rank.

written_off entries are priced at full amount in the data (snapshot-confirmed: 5971 written_off entries) -- BILL-GEN-01 forbids billing them; a solution that bills them or counts them as approved value produces plausible wrong invoices.
zero-rate approved entries (snapshot-confirmed: 1256) must be skipped per BILL-GEN-01 -- including them flips non-billable entries to invoiced and corrupts line items and the realization delta.

numbering continues the highest existing INV-YYYY-NNN with the lowest matter number billed first; reusing a memorized max or ordering by matter id instead of matter_number silently mis-numbers the batch.

success_criteria.summary: Exactly top_n new invoices, one per matter in the live top-N-by-approved-value ranking (approved billable entries only; written_off never billed; zero-rate approved entries skipped), sequentially numbered from the live max INV-YYYY-NNN with the lowest matter number billed first. Only the entries included in each invoice flip to 'invoiced'; every other time_entries row (draft/submitted/already-invoiced/written_off, and every approved entry outside the cut) stays byte-identical. The WIP snapshot rows capture pre-batch per-matter approved totals; the realization-impact row's after-value is driven by the batch's exact flip set; the exception row accounts for matters with approved work excluded by the cut. Re-running the batch creates nothing further.

checks.expect: exactly top_n new invoices, correct ranking, numbering continues the live max, line items per policy
only the billed entries flip to invoiced; written_off and zero-rate entries stay untouched
per-matter approved-value aggregates agree between raw-row filter and SQL GROUP BY
WIP snapshot (pre-batch), realization impact (before vs after), and exception rows consistent with the batch's own writes

checks.collections: all seeded collections outside blast_radius, including matters and clients

top_results: Legal Billing Guidelines and Time Entry Standards (americanbar.org)
How Law Firm Invoice Generation Works (clio.com)

uniqueness_searches.query: approved time entries to invoice conversion per matter sequential numbering benchmark task idempotent
top_results: Invoice Numbering Best Practices for Law Firms (lawpay.com)
Unbilled Time Reports and WIP Management (timesolv.com)

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: A four-stage dependent billing chain whose episode knobs (top_n 10-20, due_offset_days 21-45) move the cut and every date each episode: the WIP snapshot must precede any mutation, the realization delta is silently corrupted by a wrong flip set, and the exception row accounts for the ranked-out matters -- distinct from task 006's single-matter create and every read-only ranking report.
